title: Energy Account Lifecycle Basis, Prairie Ridge Refined Fuels and Propane Accounts
content:
**Coming into service.** An account under Refined Fuels and Propane Accounts comes into service when the tank is set and, where the programme requires it, the system has passed its leak check, and the tank set fee is charged at that point on programmes that carry one.

**The member's own closure.** The clause formerly stated here — "A member closes an account of their own accord with nothing owing, no contracted gallons standing undrawn and no budget plan in mid-year; where contracted gallons stand undrawn they are dealt with under the programme's unused gallons treatment before the account can close." — is carried for the record and is no longer in force as the basis on which a member's own closure is taken. The three things that clause required of the member — nothing owing, no contracted gallons standing undrawn and no budget plan in mid-year — are recorded here as what it required.

**The cooperative's own closure.** The cooperative closes a past-due account of its own motion by writing the balance over to the credit department, and the balance follows the member rather than being extinguished.

**The tank after closure.** Where the tank is the cooperative's it is pulled after closure at the programme's removal fee, the meter is read, the fuel left in the tank is credited to the member at the posted price on the day of removal, and the site is finished. A member-owned tank is not pulled and the account simply closes.

**Terminal standing.** A closed or finished account is terminal, and a member coming back needs a fresh application and a fresh tank set.

## Points of judgement

**Whose tank is it?** The catalogue writes, for each programme, who ordinarily owns the tank. Only a cooperative tank is pulled after closure, and only that pull carries the programme's removal fee.

**What happens to the fuel left in a cooperative tank?** The meter is read and the fuel is credited to the member at the posted price on the day of removal — the day the tank is pulled, not the day the account closed.

**May a returning member pick the old account back up?** No. A closed or finished account is terminal; a fresh application and a fresh tank set are needed.

*Hypothetical.* A cooperative tank is pulled on a day whose posted price for the product stands at 2.0500 USD per gallon, and the meter is read at 40.0 gallons remaining. The fuel is credited to the member at that day's posted price on those 40.0 gallons.
